questions.text: If γ changes from 0.9 to 0.99 in the same continuing MDP, what happens to the approximate effective reward horizon?

options.A: It shrinks from about 100 steps to about 10 steps.
options.B: It stays near 10 steps because the policy is unchanged.
options.C: It becomes infinite because γ is close to 1.
options.D: It grows from about 10 steps to about 100 steps.

questions.explanation: The effective horizon is roughly 1/(1−γ): γ=0.9 gives about 10 steps and γ=0.99 gives about 100.

questions.text: A warehouse agent is rewarded only when every order is fulfilled at the end of a long shift. It rarely sees a successful episode. Which change directly addresses this sparse-reward problem?

options.A: Remove state information so the agent explores more broadly.
options.B: Add useful intermediate rewards tied to progress toward fulfilled orders.
options.C: Set γ=0 so the final outcome no longer affects early actions.
options.D: Increase the size of the terminal reward without changing when feedback arrives.

questions.explanation: Intermediate reward shaping tied to the target outcome provides more frequent learning signals when terminal success is rare.

questions.text: The GridWorld starts at (0,0). A deterministic policy moves right, right, right, down, down, down into terminal (3,3), receiving -1 on each move. With γ=1 for this finite episode, what is the rollout’s total return?

options.A: -3, because only the horizontal moves count.
options.B: -5, because entering the terminal gives no reward.
options.C: -6, because all six moves each give reward -1.
options.D: 0, because γ=1 cancels the step penalties.

questions.explanation: There are six transitions from (0,0) to (3,3), and entering the terminal still incurs -1; with γ=1, the total is -6.
